proofs.full_local_argument: Let P_+ and P_- be the laws conditional on S=+1 and S=-1. For one label, KL(P_+||P_-)=theta log((1+theta)/(1-theta)). Since log((1+theta)/(1-theta))=integral_{-theta}^{theta}(1+x)^{-1} dx <=2theta/(1-theta)<=4theta, this KL is at most 4theta^2. Conditional independence gives KL between the first r-1 label laws at most 4(r-1)theta^2. Appending Z leaves this KL unchanged because its law is the same independent factor under both signs. Pinsker therefore bounds TV of the available histories by sqrt(2(r-1)) theta <=sqrt(2n theta^2)<=1/4. Under equal sign priors every binary test based on that history has error probability at least (1-TV)/2>=3/8. Define the test to be +1 when X_r>=0 and -1 otherwise. On a test error |X_r-S theta|>=theta, including the tie case X_r=0. Thus E[(X_r-S theta)^2]>=3theta^2/8 for every r. Summing yields the asserted bound. No learner randomness can improve it, since all independent randomization was included in Z.
map: Compute one-label KL between the two sign models.
Bound history TV by Pinsker, retaining independent auxiliary randomness.
Apply binary testing risk to sign(X_r), then sum squared-risk contributions.

assumptions: No prediction uses its current or future label.
Observations from other hidden coordinates may be included in Z only when independent of (S,Y_1:n).
statement.conclusion: sum_{r=1}^n E[(X_r-S theta)^2]>=c n theta^2 for a universal c>0; the supplied argument gives c=3/8.
statement.objects_and_definitions: S is uniform on {-1,+1}. Conditional on S, Y_1,...,Y_n in {-1,+1} are independent with P(Y_r=1|S)=(1+S theta)/2. Let Z be auxiliary randomness independent of the joint vector (S,Y_1,...,Y_n). X_r in [-1,1] is measurable with respect to (Y_1,...,Y_{r-1},Z).
statement.parameter_domains: n is a positive integer; 0<theta<=1/2; n theta^2<=1/32.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every n, theta and every such possibly randomized sequential prediction process, expectation over S, labels and auxiliary randomness satisfies the conclusion.

facets.subject: Only prior labels and jointly independent auxiliary randomness

research_use.reason: Small history KL forces constant sign-test error at each prediction.

summary: With n theta^2<=1/32, any past-label sequential predictor has cumulative expected squared error at least (3/8)n theta^2.
